title: Monitoring the growth of Solanum betaceum non-embryogenic callus using EIS
author: Caeiro, Canhoto, et al.
materials: Corning Falcon cell culture plate (12 wells)

Timing: 3–4 h
1.Prepare solutions of KOH (1 M and 0.1 M).a.Dissolve 5.611 g of KOH in 100 mL of distilled water (1 M solution).b.Dilute 10 mL of KOH 1 M in 90 mL of distilled water (0.1 M solution).2.Prepare solutions of HCl (1 M and 0.1 M).a.Add 82 mL of HCl 37% to 918 mL of distilled water (1 M solution).b.Dilute 10 mL of HCl 1 M in 90 mL of distilled water (0.1 M solution).
CRITICAL: Concentrated HCl should be handled in a fume hood with protective gear and extreme caution.
3.Prepare a stock solution of picloram (1 mg/mL).a.Dissolve 100 mg of picloram in 1 mL of NaOH 1 M.b.Transfer 1 ml of picloram solution to about 30 mL of distilled water under agitation.c.Adjust the volume to 100 mL.d.Store at −20°C for further use up to a month.4.Prepare calcium hypochlorite solution (50 g/L).a.Dissolve 10 g of calcium hypochlorite in 200 mL of distilled water.b.Filter the solution (Whatman paper #1).
Note: The calcium hypochlorite solution should be used immediately.
5.Prepare acetocarmine 1% (w/v) staining solution.a.Mix 45 mL of glacial acetic acid in 55 mL of distilled water.b.Heat the acetic acid solution in a 1 L Erlenmeyer flash until starts boiling.c.Add 1 g of acetocarmine to the acetic acid solution and maintain the temperature at approximately 95°C for 5 min.d.Let the solution reach room temperature (20°C).e.Filter the solution with a Whatman paper #1 into a dark container.
Note: Acetocarmine solution can be stored for up to 2 years. However, if a precipitate is observed, a filtration step similar to e. should be done before using.
CRITICAL: Steps b and c should be performed under a fume hood.
6.Prepare fluorescein diacetate staining solution (2 μg/mL).a.Dissolve 100 mg of fluorescein diacetate in 100 mL acetone (stock solution – 1 mg/mL).b.Dissolve 9 g of sucrose in 100 ml of distilled water (dilution solution).c.Add 20 μL ml of stock solution in 9.8 mL of dilution solution (final volume of 10 mL).
Note: The stock solution can be stored at −20°C for at least 3 months. The dilution and staining solution should be prepared immediately before use.
CRITICAL: Acetone is highly flammable and should be handled under a fume hood.
7.Prepare germination medium (half-strength MS medium supplemented with 0.29 mM sucrose).a.Dissolve 10 g of sucrose in 800 mL of distilled water.b.Add 2.2 g of Murashige and Skoog medium including vitamins to 800 mL of distilled water with sucrose.c.Adjust the pH to 5.6–5.8 with KOH (0.1 or 1.0 M) or HCl (0.1 or 1 M) solutions.d.Add 7 g of plant agar.e.Adjust the volume to 1 L.f.Autoclave at 121°C for 20 min.8.Prepare micropropagation medium (MS medium supplemented with 0.09 M sucrose and 0.88 μM BAP).a.Dissolve 30 g of sucrose in 800 mL of distilled water.b.Add 4.4 g of Murashige and Skoog medium including vitamins to 800 mL of distilled water with sucrose.c.Add 200 μL of BAP stock solution.d.Adjust the pH to 5.6–5.8 with KOH or HCl solutions.e.Add 7 g of plant agar.f.Adjust the volume to 1 L.g.Autoclave at 121°C for 20 min.9.Prepare auxin-rich medium (MS supplemented with 0.26 M sucrose and 20 μM picloram).a.Dissolve 90 g of sucrose in 800 mL of distilled water.b.Add 4.4 g of Murashige and Skoog medium including vitamins to 800 mL of distilled water with sucrose.c.Add 5 ml of picloram stock solution.d.Adjust the pH to 5.6-5-8 with KOH or HCl solutions.e.Add 2.5 g of Phytagel.f.Adjust the volume to 1 L.g.Autoclave at 121°C for 20 min.10.Prepare auxin-free medium (MS supplemented with 26 mM sucrose).a.Dissolve 90 g of sucrose in 800 mL of distilled water.b.Add 4.4 g of Murashige and Skoog medium including vitamins to 800 mL of distilled water with sucrose.c.Adjust the pH to 5.6-5-8 with KOH or HCl solutions.d.Add 2.5 g of Phytagel.e.Adjust the volume to 1 L.f.Autoclave at 121°C for 20 min.
CRITICAL: The medium should be distributed to the final container (Petri dishes, microplates or EIS apparatus) immediately after autoclaving at a temperature of about 60°C. Furthermore, if thermolabile compounds are being tested (such as some auxin polar transport inhibitors), the stock solution should be sterilized by filtration (0.2 μm pore filter) and an appropriate volume added at this stage.

The impedance modulus and phase over the full frequency spectrum, from 1 Hz to 1 MHz, is first examined to verify the relaxation frequency of the electrochemical system, which can vary with electrode area, material and solution resistance (see Figures 4B and 4C). After this stage, impedance modulus at 10 Hz (|Z|), before the relaxation frequency,10 can be traced as a function of time and related to mass increase. Thus, mass increase should also be represented as a function of time. Both parameters are expected to present an exponential increase phase between 24 h to 72 h (see expected results). In this phase, the rate of increase can be calculated as:(Equation 1)ri=Vf−Vitf−tiWhere ri is the rate, Vf and Vi are the |Z| modulus or mass and tf an ti are the corresponding times, respectively. The rate will have units of Ω/h or mg/h for |Z| and mass increase, respectively. A similar analysis can be used for Rct and Rsol when plotted over time.

The goodness of fit of any ri can be tested using coefficient of determination or a similar metric. Furthermore, mass and impedance values can be normalized between 0 and 1:(Equation 2)Xn=X−XminXmax−XminWhere Xn is the normalized value, X is the original data point and Xmin and Xmax are the minimal and maximum values, respectively. Impedance and mass values can then be analyzed by a correlation test (e.g. Pearson correlation test).

steps.title: Prepare KOH stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 1 M KOH by dissolving 5.611 g KOH in 100 mL distilled water; make 0.1 M KOH by diluting 10 mL of the 1 M solution into 90 mL distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare HCl stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 M HCl by adding 82 mL of 37 % HCl to 918 mL distilled water; prepare 0.1 M HCl by diluting 10 mL of the 1 M solution into 90 mL distilled water. Handle concentrated HCl in a fume hood with protective gear.

steps.title: Prepare picloram stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg picloram in 1 mL 1 M NaOH; transfer to ~30 mL distilled water under agitation; bring volume to 100 mL; store at –20 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare calcium hypochlorite solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g calcium hypochlorite in 200 mL distilled water (final 50 g L⁻¹); filter through Whatman paper #1; use the solution immediately.

steps.title: Prepare acetocarmine staining solution
steps.instruction: Mix 45 mL glacial acetic acid with 55 mL distilled water; heat the mixture in a 1 L Erlenmeyer flask until it starts boiling; add 1 g acetocarmine and keep at ~95 °C for 5 min; let cool to room temperature (20 °C); filter through Whatman paper #1 into a dark container. Store up to 2 years; if precipitate appears, filter again. Perform heating steps under a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescein diacetate staining solution
steps.instruction: Make a 1 mg mL⁻¹ stock by dissolving 100 mg fluorescein diacetate in 100 mL acetone (store at –20 °C ≥3 months). Prepare a 9 % (w/v) sucrose dilution by dissolving 9 g sucrose in 100 mL distilled water. Add 20 µL of the stock to 9.8 mL of the sucrose solution to obtain 10 mL of 2 µg mL⁻¹ fluorescein diacetate staining solution. Prepare the dilution immediately before use. Handle acetone in a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare germination medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g sucrose in 800 mL distilled water; add 2.2 g Murashige & Skoog (MS) salts with vitamins; adjust pH to 5.6–5.8 with 0.1 M or 1 M KOH or HCl; add 7 g plant agar; bring volume to 1 L; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare micropropagation medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 30 g sucrose in 800 mL distilled water; add 4.4 g MS salts with vitamins; add 200 µL BAP stock solution; adjust pH to 5.6–5.8 with KOH or HCl (0.1 M or 1 M); add 7 g plant agar; bring volume to 1 L; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare auxin‑rich medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 90 g sucrose in 800 mL distilled water; add 4.4 g MS salts with vitamins; add 5 mL picloram stock (20 µM final); adjust pH to 5.6–5.8 with KOH or HCl; add 2.5 g Phytagel; bring volume to 1 L; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare auxin‑free medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 90 g sucrose in 800 mL distilled water; add 4.4 g MS salts with vitamins; adjust pH to 5.6–5.8 with KOH or HCl; add 2.5 g Phytagel; bring volume to 1 L; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Distribute medium after autoclaving
steps.instruction: While still warm (~60 °C), pour the sterilized medium into the final containers (Petri dishes, microplates or EIS apparatus). For thermolabile compounds, filter‑sterilize stock solutions (0.2 µm) and add the appropriate volume at this stage.

steps.title: Bright‑field microscopy of NEC
steps.instruction: Remove a minimal NEC sample from auxin‑rich medium; place on a glass slide; add 2–3 drops of 1 % acetocarmine solution; cover with a coverslip; observe with a Nikon Eclipse Ci microscope (40×/0.65 NA Plan Achromat objective) equipped with a Nikon DS‑Fi3 camera; process images with NIS‑Elements D v4.60. Repeat at desired time points (e.g., days 3 and 7) for both auxin‑rich and auxin‑free samples.

steps.title: Scanning electron microscopy of NEC
steps.instruction: Remove a minimal NEC sample from auxin‑rich medium; mount on a metallic SEM stub using double‑sided conductive carbon tape; place the stub in a variable‑pressure SEM (Flex SEM 1000, Hitachi) in low‑vacuum mode; set acquisition parameters: 15 kV accelerating voltage, 6.7 mm working distance, BSE‑COMP signal, 210× magnification, scan speed 80, resolution 1280 × 960 px; repeat for the same time‑point samples and for auxin‑free samples.

steps.title: Fluorescein diacetate viability assay
steps.instruction: For each condition, place ~20 mg NEC in a 1.5 mL vial. Control: add 1 mL diluting solution (no fluorescein), vortex 30 s, place 2–3 drops on a slide, cover with a coverslip. Test: add 1 mL fluorescein diacetate (2 µg mL⁻¹) solution, vortex 30 s, incubate 5 min in the dark at 15–20 °C, place 2–3 drops on a slide, cover. Repeat the whole procedure for NEC from auxin‑free medium and for the same time‑point samples used in step 5. Observe slides with an Axio Image.Z2 microscope (Plan‑Apochromat 20×/0.8 NA, AxioCam HRm3); excite at 450–490 nm, collect emission at 500–550 nm; acquire images with ZEN 3.2 (Blue) at 20×, 300 ms exposure, 58.3 % light intensity, 14‑bit depth; process images in Fiji (auto‑adjust brightness/contrast, measure raw integrated density).

steps.title: Impedance‑mass correlation analysis
steps.instruction: Plot impedance modulus |Z| at 10 Hz versus time and mass versus time; calculate rate ri = (Vf‑Vi)/(tf‑ti) for each interval (units Ω h⁻¹ or mg h⁻¹); assess goodness‑of‑fit with coefficient of determination; normalize values Xn = (X‑Xmin)/(Xmax‑Xmin); perform Pearson correlation between normalized impedance and mass; optionally repeat analysis for Rct and Rsol.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of image data
steps.instruction: Measure pore areas on SEM micrographs using Fiji’s scale tool; obtain raw integrated density from fluorescence images; test variance homogeneity with Brown‑Forsythe; if variances are homogeneous, conduct ANOVA followed by Tukey’s multiple‑comparison test; if not, use Kruskal‑Wallis followed by Dunn’s test; report significance levels.

steps.title: Equivalent circuit fitting
steps.instruction: Import impedance spectra into fitting software (e.g., Zview); fit data to the double RC circuit model described in the protocol; extract charge‑transfer resistance (Rct) and solution resistance (Rsol); interpret differences between auxin‑rich and auxin‑free conditions in relation to cell physiology.
